title: Transformations
description: Animated KS3 Maths lesson on transformations for ages 9 to 14: reflection in a mirror line, translation, rotation about a centre, enlargement by a scale factor, congruent shapes, line symmetry and rotational symmetry, with coordinates on a grid.
intro: Flip it, slide it, turn it or make it bigger: reflections, translations, rotations, enlargements and symmetry, explained by the owl in six short parts.

chapters.title: Four ways to move a shape

steps.say: A **transformation** changes where a shape is, which way it faces, or how big it is.
There are four kinds. A **reflection** flips. A **rotation** turns. A **translation** slides. An **enlargement** makes a shape bigger or smaller.
After a reflection, rotation or translation, the new shape is exactly the same size and shape. We say it is **congruent**. Only an enlargement changes the size.

check.q: Which transformation can change the size of a shape?
check.hint: Flipping, turning and sliding all keep the shape the same size. Which one is left?
check.explain: Only an **enlargement** changes the size. Reflections, rotations and translations give a congruent shape: same size, same shape.

steps.say: A **reflection** flips a shape over a **mirror line**. Here the mirror line is the y-axis.
Every corner of the image is the **same distance** from the mirror line as the corner it came from, but on the other side. This corner is 4 squares from the line on each side.
Reflect the point (3, 2) in the y-axis and it goes to (−3, 2). The **x-coordinate changes sign**. The y-coordinate stays the same.
steps.speak: Reflect the point 3, 2 in the y-axis and it goes to negative 3, 2. The x-coordinate changes sign. The y-coordinate stays the same.

steps.say: Now the mirror line is the x-axis. The point (4, 3) goes to (4, −3). This time the **y-coordinate changes sign**.
steps.speak: Now the mirror line is the x-axis. The point 4, 3 goes to 4, negative 3. This time the y-coordinate changes sign.

check.q: The point (5, 2) is reflected in the y-axis. Where does it go?
check.hint: The y-axis is the up-and-down line. The point jumps from the right side to the left side. Which coordinate changes?
check.explain: Reflecting in the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate: (5, 2) → **(−5, 2)**.

steps.say: A **translation** slides a shape. It does not turn or flip.
**Every point** moves the same distance in the same direction. Here each corner moves 5 squares right and 2 squares down.
With coordinates: moving right adds to x, left takes away from x. Up adds to y, down takes away from y. So (1, 2) moved 3 right and 2 up goes to (4, 4).
steps.speak: With coordinates: moving right adds to x, left takes away from x. Up adds to y, down takes away from y. So 1, 2 moved 3 right and 2 up goes to 4, 4.

steps.say: The image is **congruent**: the same size and shape, and it still faces the same way.

check.q: The point (5, 2) is translated 3 squares left and 1 square down. Where does it go?
check.hint: Left takes away from x. Down takes away from y.
check.explain: x: 5 − 3 = 2. y: 2 − 1 = 1. So the point goes to **(2, 1)**.

steps.say: A **rotation** turns a shape. A quarter turn is 90°. A half turn is 180°. A full turn is 360°.
steps.speak: A rotation turns a shape. A quarter turn is 90 degrees. A half turn is 180 degrees. A full turn is 360 degrees.

steps.say: To describe a rotation, give three things: the **angle**, the **direction** (clockwise or anticlockwise) and the **centre**, the point it turns about.
This triangle turns 90° clockwise about the origin, (0, 0). Every point turns around the centre by the same angle.
steps.speak: This triangle turns 90 degrees clockwise about the origin, 0, 0. Every point turns around the centre by the same angle.

steps.say: A half turn about the origin changes the sign of **both** coordinates. (3, 1) goes to (−3, −1).
steps.speak: A half turn about the origin changes the sign of both coordinates. 3, 1 goes to negative 3, negative 1.

check.q: The point (0, 3) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. Where does it go?
check.hint: The point is on the y-axis, 3 squares up. Turn it a quarter turn the way a clock's hands go.
check.explain: A quarter turn clockwise takes a point that is 3 up round to 3 to the right: **(3, 0)**.

steps.say: An **enlargement** changes the size. The **scale factor** tells you how many times bigger. With scale factor 3, a 2 by 1 rectangle becomes 6 by 3.
To find the scale factor, divide: **new length ÷ old length**. Here 6 ÷ 2 = 3. The angles stay the same.
steps.speak: To find the scale factor, divide the new length by the old length. Here 6 divided by 2 equals 3. The angles stay the same.

steps.say: An enlargement can have a **centre**. With scale factor 2, every corner ends up twice as far from the centre as before.
Watch out for area! With scale factor 2, the length and the width both double, so the area is 2 × 2 = 4 times bigger.
steps.speak: Watch out for area! With scale factor 2, the length and the width both double, so the area is 2 times 2, which is 4 times bigger.

check.q: A rectangle 4 cm by 3 cm is enlarged by scale factor 2. What are its new measurements?
check.hint: Multiply every length by the scale factor.
check.explain: 4 × 2 = 8 cm and 3 × 2 = 6 cm, so the new rectangle is **8 cm by 6 cm**.

steps.say: A shape has **line symmetry** if you can fold it along a line and the two halves match exactly. That line is a **line of symmetry**.
An equilateral triangle has **3** lines of symmetry. A square has **4**.
**Rotational symmetry**: turn the shape. Count how many times it fits onto itself in one full turn. A square fits 4 times, so its **order** is 4.
The letter S and a parallelogram both fit onto themselves after a half turn: order 2. A parallelogram has **no** lines of symmetry at all.

check.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle (that is not a square) have?
check.hint: Imagine folding a sheet of paper. Which folds make the halves match? A diagonal fold does not!
check.explain: A rectangle has **2** lines of symmetry: one across the middle and one down the middle. The diagonals are not lines of symmetry.
